nodes.answer: The first Global Assessment was approved at IPBES-7.

nodes.question: What was the location and date of the eleventh session of IPBES?
nodes.answer: The eleventh session of IPBES was held in Windhoek, Namibia, in December 2024.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|United nations climate change conferences (cops)_qna_002
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What were the two main assessments approved during the IPBES-11 plenary?
nodes.answer: The two main assessments approved were the Nexus Assessment and the Transformative Change Assessment.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|United nations climate change conferences (cops)_qna_003
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What was the average annual frequency of MHW events across all sites?
nodes.answer: The average annual frequency of MHW events across all sites was 2.23 events per year.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|United nations climate change conferences (cops)_qna_004
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What shift in focus has occurred in discussions regarding energy at COP events over time?
nodes.answer: Discussions have increasingly included fossil fuel phase-out topics, growing from limited early discourse to nearly half of all energy events since COP17, reflecting rising anti-fossil fuel sentiment.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|United nations climate change conferences (cops)_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Which topics have shown significant changes in discussion at COP events from 2003 to 2023 according to the analysis in the article?
nodes.answer: Discussions on energy have evolved with an increase in fossil fuel discourse, while forest management topics have halved, and food-related topics have shifted towards broader perspectives on food systems and resilience.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|United nations climate change conferences (cops)_qna_006
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What are the primary focuses of discussions at COP side events from 2003 to 2023?
nodes.answer: The primary focuses of discussions at COP side events include energy topics, forest management, and food and agriculture systems, with energy discussions covering areas such as renewable energy, fossil fuels, bio-energy, nuclear energy, and energy poverty.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|United nations climate change conferences (cops)_qna_007
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How has the discourse on fossil fuels evolved at COP side events since COP17?
nodes.answer: Since COP17 in 2011, the discourse on fossil fuels has increased to nearly half of all energy events, covering various issues such as fossil fuel subsidy reform and phase-out, reflecting growing anti-fossil fuel sentiment.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|United nations climate change conferences (cops)_qna_008
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How has the discourse around fossil fuels changed since the early years of COP conferences according to the findings?
nodes.answer: The fossil fuel discourse at COP conferences has increased significantly from the early years, escalating to nearly half of all energy events since COP17 in 2011. This change reflects rising criticism of high-polluting nations and industries, and discussions now encompass various facets such as subsidy reform and phase-out strategies.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|United nations climate change conferences (cops)_qna_009
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the primary focuses of the side events at the UNFCCC COPs from 2003 to 2023?
nodes.answer: The primary focuses of the side events include energy (especially renewable energy), forest management, and food and agriculture systems, with energy discussions being particularly emphasized.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|United nations climate change conferences (cops)_qna_010
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How have the discussions surrounding fossil fuels changed in COP side events from the early years to recent years?
nodes.answer: Discussions surrounding fossil fuels have increased dramatically, moving from limited early discourse to nearly half of all energy events by 2023, reflecting growing anti-fossil fuel sentiment and criticism of high-polluting nations and corporations.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|United nations climate change conferences (cops)_qna_011
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What are the three most common topics identified in side events during UNFCCC from 2003 to 2023?
nodes.answer: The three most common topics identified are forest management, renewable energy, and food and agriculture systems.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|United nations climate change conferences (cops)_qna_012
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How has access to UNFCCC COP events for fossil fuel lobbyists been facilitated according to the analysis?
nodes.answer: Fossil fuel lobbyists gain access through nominations from developed-country business NGOs and developing-country governments.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|United nations climate change conferences (cops)_qna_013
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What are the main topics of discussion in side events at UNFCCC COPs from 2003 to 2023?
nodes.answer: The three most common topics discussed in side events are forest management, renewable energy, and food and agriculture systems, with a total of 63 distinct topics identified.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|United nations climate change conferences (cops)_qna_014
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How have energy discussions at COP side events evolved over time?
nodes.answer: Energy discussions have fluctuated between 5% to 10% of side events, with a growing focus on renewable energy while fossil fuel discussions increased to nearly half of all energy events since COP17 (2011).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|United nations climate change conferences (cops)_qna_015
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What role do non-state actors play in the UNFCCC process?
nodes.answer: Non-state actors, while not directly involved in decision-making, contribute informally by sharing expertise and influencing broader discourse through side events, pavilion events, and informal meetings.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|United nations climate change conferences (cops)_qna_016
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What has been a major avenue for non-state actor engagement in UNFCCC processes, particularly through COPs?
nodes.answer: Side events have been a major avenue for non-state actor engagement, facilitating knowledge transfer and capacity building, and increasing the legitimacy and acceptance of the UNFCCC process.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|United nations climate change conferences (cops)_qna_017
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How has the discourse around fossil fuels and renewable energy changed at COP side events from the early 2000s to 2023?
nodes.answer: Initially, fossil fuel discussions were limited but have increased significantly, constituting nearly half of all energy events since COP17 (2011), while renewable energy consistently remained a prominent topic.
